final.memo:
Our investment in the Company, thesis-ed on a turnaround following the distribution suspension, is being severely tested by management's inability to execute. Recent results confirm that the centralization of service and dispatch was a disaster, leading to annual attrition of 6.5%—a staggering increase from 1.3% in fiscal 2003 [D02], [D03]. With retail volume falling 14.9% and losses mounting, the current leadership has provided no credible path to stabilize the franchise [D03], [D07].

We have historically engaged privately, but our patience is not infinite when the business is hemorrhaging customers and margins are under extreme pressure from wholesale cost volatility [D03], [D08]. The propane sale, while providing liquidity, does not excuse the lack of operational focus; furthermore, with 10.25% notes and restrictive covenants in place, the margin for error is razor-thin [D02], [D04]. Secured creditors are positioned to capture value should this decline continue, leaving little for the common unitholders [D04], [D05].

We are moving to ESCALATE. We will not sit by while management hides behind stale guidance and fails to address the underlying structural rot in the distribution business. The next few months, covering the tail end of the peak heating season and the use-of-proceeds window, are critical [D03], [D07]. If the board is unwilling to implement a swift turnaround and leadership change, we will take our case directly to the other unitholders to ensure this asset is managed for value rather than further destruction [D07], [D08].
